name: Simile
summary: Simile develops synthetic users for product and market research, using AI agents to simulate audience behavior and feedback.
overview: Simile offers synthetic users for marketing and product research. In July 2026, the company announced a $200 million Series B at a $2 billion valuation, five months after a $100 million Series A.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Simile reportedly raised more than $200 million in Series B funding at a $2 billion valuation.

bull_case: If synthetic panels become reliable enough for iterative research, they can materially shorten the feedback loop for product and marketing teams.
bear_case: Synthetic outputs can encode weak assumptions or produce misleading confidence, limiting adoption in decisions that require representative human evidence.
latest_round: Reported July 2026 Series B: $200M+ at a $2B valuation
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

intelligence.description: An AI research platform built around simulated users for product and market research.
company: Simile uses AI agents to simulate users for product and market research. The company positions the platform as a faster complement to conventional research workflows, where teams need repeated feedback on messaging, concepts, and product decisions.

The company announced a $200 million Series B at a $2 billion valuation in July 2026, led by Greenoaks. It followed a $100 million Series A announced five months earlier, making the pace of financing itself a notable part of the profile.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Synthetic research is an emerging application layer for AI, where value depends on whether simulated behavior is decision-useful rather than merely convincing. Simile is a high-profile private-market test of that proposition.

changed.text: Simile announced a $200M Series B at a $2B valuation, led by Greenoaks.

takeaways: The July 2026 Series B set a $2B valuation only months after the Series A.
The investment case rests on the reliability of simulated research outputs.
Methodological trust and customer retention are the central open questions.
